trajectory_summary: The call opens with a soft refusal, gets pulled toward genuine curiosity by three separate cost questions, but the rep never converts that curiosity into qualification or a scheduled appointment. The call ends with the customer promising to email in a week and the rep sending only a personal number/email — no date, time, or verify data captured.
outcome_dispute: If v1 tagged this as any form of booked/tentative appointment, that is miscalled — no date or time was ever set; the customer explicitly deferred to emailing 'in a week' with no rep-owned follow-up mechanism beyond a text with personal contact info.

observed_outcome.quote: I just I'll email you, in a week.
observed_outcome.reasoning: No specific day or time was ever agreed upon; the customer deferred to emailing at an unspecified point in the future, and the rep's only action was sending a text with personal contact info — there is no rep-owned next step with a fixed date.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked for utility company or average bill amount at any point in the call; the only financial figures discussed were the customer's repeated general cost questions, which the rep answered with tax-incentive framing rather than gathering a bill number.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked what interested the customer in solar; the customer volunteered general cost curiosity and a home-size detail but never stated a specific motivating reason (bill pain, environment, etc.), and the rep did not probe for one.

script_coverage.quote: Hey, Bobby. This is Carter calling from ION. I see that you requested some more information on solar for your home.
Does the the government credit, does that pay for a lot of it?

primary_coaching_focus.topic: unanchored soft exit — no date/time locked
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I just I'll email you, in a week.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer asked pricing questions three separate times, showing real interest, but the call ends with zero appointment mechanics (no day, no time, no handshake) — this is the single biggest value leak on the call and the most fixable with a specific script drill.

key_moments.quote: Not really interested right now, but I'll, if I do, I'll get with you.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is squarely the hello-objection pattern — customer distancing within the opening moments. The script calls for an acknowledge-then-small-ask response.

key_moments.quote: Give me a ballpark figure on what it cost.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a direct match for the price_estimate_before_design rebuttal, which is designed to trade the answer for the verify info needed to build a real design. The rep answers generically instead of trading.

key_moments.quote: There's not a very big house. I mean, it's, 2,000 square foot.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers a concrete home-size detail unprompted — a natural entry point to start the verify conversation (roof, bill, utility) and build toward a real estimate. Rep just says 'Okay' and lets the moment pass.

key_moments.quote: Can I reach you back at this number?
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the pivot point where the call needed a firm time anchor (protocols.time_constraint) and instead the rep let the customer set the terms of re-contact.
